item.title: Re: Living on repeat
item.content:encoded:
I guess my biggest concern here is: what are you actually going to do with this narratively?

Like, there's a lot of interesting thematic stuff, and choosing to tell this story from the outside looking in is an interesting choice (even if I am concerned that it adds a big separation from the emotional core of the story), but I don't really have a feel for what actually like…happens here? We see all these loops and touch on them briefly or w/e but how do they all add together? What makes this into a coherent whole of a story with a beginning/middle/end and rising tension and a climax and all the stuff we expect to see?

item.title: Living on repeat
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Emotional, Time-loop, Thought provoking

Elevator Pitch: Imagine Groundhogs day, but it's your whole life start to finish, over and over, with seemingly no end. You're still a human otherwise, and can only remember so much at a time. Now imagine a character with that life, who is looking for a way out of what he views as the worst form of immortality. That's SCP-XXXX.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is a regular male who is quantum looped, resulting in him reliving his life over and over from start to finish. Their choices through life cause butterfly effects that can sometimes have unforeseen consequences, causing his futures to always shift in different ways as the effects of his compiled choices ripple outwards in a butterfly effect. He's learned to navigate this to a degree by condensing the core lessons of his lives into his earliest years each life, doing his best to hold onto the important lessons he's learned while trying to navigate to an end to this exhausting mental tightrope.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Time-loops like Ground Hogs day have been done, but generally following the perspective of the one going through the loop. This is written from the perspective of an exclusion site, that is removed from the butterfly effects but receive multiple, usually near-identical reports every time a document is uploaded in regards to SCP-XXXX. This could be an interview log, incident report, or other seemingly unrelated log where his actions changed the contents. It would be a small window into a life that has been lived in so many different ways, over and over again.

Additional Notes: This guy isn't a "Gary Stu", in that he can't master every skill in the cosmos, isn't built like a Greek god, and certainly isn't universally loved. He claims to have "streamlined childhood", and as a result has certain skills he practices in every lifetime. He struggles to relate to other humans, as it's very clear to him that no one else is remembering anything from life to life. The fact that the Foundation can record his activities in other lives interests him greatly, and he sees it as a way to gain assistance in stopping "his eternal hamster wheel". He doesn't mind when sometimes the Foundation may utilize his anomalous property un-ethically or insensitively, as he believes he's self contained and can "leave" whenever.
